messages.author: 894b142904c60979
messages.subject: Open distance sampling models
parts:
Hi all,
I am attempting to run an open hierarchical distance sampling model using gdistsamp() and I have a couple of questions on how to treat my data.I am relatively new to this so forgive me if these answers are obvious. 

I surveyed fireflies using distance sampling at 10 point transects 3-9 times each over the summer. During each night, at each point, I conducted 5, 1-minute firefly surveys (to try to limit double counting/having to keep track of individuals for more than a minute). Therefore, individual fireflies were counted anew during each 1-minute survey, for 5 minutes. 

1) I have created an effort matrix that shows which points (n = 10) were surveyed during which weeks (n = 9). However, I am unsure how to bring in the within-night replicates to account for the 5, 1-minute surveys that were conducted at each point, each night. Survey-level covariates were only collected once per point per night, but distances to fireflies were measured within 5 surveys (each being 1-min). 

2) I never detected fireflies at one of my points. Despite adding a level for the point with no detections into my detections data (using (levels(dist_data$pt_id) <- c(levels(dist_data$pt_id), levels(ptNoObs$pt_id)))), the formatDistData() function results in a matrix with 9 rows, rather than 10. This later becomes an issue since I have covariates for all 10 points and I get an error when trying to run the model. How do I address this?

yDat <- formatDistData(dist_data,
                 distCol = "dist_m",
                 transectNameCol = "point_index",
                 dist.breaks = breaks,
                 occasionCol = "week",
                 effortMatrix = effortMatrix)

Thank you in advance for any help you can provide!

Rachel

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Open distance sampling models
parts:
Hi Rachel,

Have you tried creating the data using unmarkedFrameGDS() directly, instead of using formatDistData? I would recommend doing that instead, for complete control over the structure of your dataset. I think you may have one more level of organization than unmarked can handle, though. It sounds like you have distance bins nested inside surveys nested inside weeks for each site. But gdistsamp() can only handle two levels of "hierarchy" (e.g. distance bins inside surveys, or distance bins with repeat weeks). I guess one option would be pooling observations across surveys within weeks.

Ken

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Open distance sampling models
parts:
On closer reading I guess pooling across surveys does not make sense since you are counting the same fireflies each time. So options could be

1) Only use one of the 5 repeat surveys per week, and then the repeat occasions in the model are the weeks
2) Make a "site" in your analysis actually a site-week, and then the repeat occasions are the repeat surveys within that site-week. In this case you are possibly psuedoreplicating sites.

Ken

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Open distance sampling models
parts:
I agree with Ken's ideas for dealing with the multiple samples.
Regarding the site with 0 detections, the matrix of distance class counts should have a row of all zero entries to indicate 0 individuals caught in each distance class. You might have to do this explicitly by augmenting yDat with a row of all zero values.
